title: Finiteness of the concrete normalization at a generic boundary point
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral Noetherian quasi-separated scheme, $c:C\to S$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated smooth morphism with geometrically connected fibres, and $G$ a finite group whose order is invertible in $\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $q:C_\eta\to\operatorname{Spec} k(S)$ and $j:C_\eta\to C$ exhibit the generic fibre, and let $Z\to C_\eta$ be a finite etale $G$-torsor. Let $U\subset S$ be open containing $\eta$, let $P\to C_U$ be finite etale, and let $j_U:C_\eta\to C_U$ and $\psi:Z\to P$ exhibit its generic restriction, with $i_Uj_U=j$, where $i_U:C_U\to C$ is the open inclusion [def-pc-fibre-product]. Fix $s\notin U$ such that every $t\notin U$ specializing to $s$ equals $s$. Set $f:P\to C$ to be the composite with $i_U$, let $N\to C$ be its concrete relative normalization (on each affine chart the integral closure of the base ring in the sections of $P$), and let $L=C\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s}$ with projection $l:L\to C$. Then $N\times_C L\to L$ is finite. No section or rational section-fibre point is assumed.

proof.text: If C is empty, the local total space is empty and the normalization pullback map is an isomorphism, hence finite.

For nonempty C apply smooth_connected_generic_geometry_core to get integrality and integrally closed stalks. Smoothness implies locally finite type, and quasi-compactness over the Noetherian S gives IsNoetherian C by Mathlib isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType.

For f=PA.obj.hom composed with the open inclusion into C, apply the finite affine integral-closure lemma on every affine V of C. Mathlib fromNormalization_app and normalizationObjIso identify the normalization ring map with the finite structural algebra map followed by an isomorphism. The IsFinite constructor glues these affine conclusions into global finiteness of f.fromNormalization.

Pull back this finite normalization along pullback.fst c (S.fromSpecStalk s). Mathlib finiteness under base change gives exactly the original conclusion. No compatibility theorem for normalization and localization is needed: the given normalization is already globally finite.

theorem GaloisCover.stalk_normalization_finite {S C : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian S]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [IsIntegral S]
    (hS : ∀ x : S, IsIntegrallyClosed (S.presheaf.stalk x))
    (c : C ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact c] [QuasiSeparated c] [Smooth c] [GeometricallyConnected c]
    (G : Type (u + 1)) [Group G] [Finite G]
    (hG : IsUnit (Nat.card G : Γ(S, ⊤)))
    {Cη : Scheme.{u}} (q : Cη ⟶ Spec S.functionField) (j : Cη ⟶ C)
    (hCη : IsPullback q j (S.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint S)) c)
    (Z : GaloisCover G Cη)
    (U : S.Opens) (hηU : genericPoint S ∈ U)
    (jU : Cη ⟶ (c ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme) (PA : (c ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme.FiniteEtale)
    (ψ : Z.P ⟶ PA.obj.left) (hjU : jU ≫ (c ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι = j)
    (hψ : IsPullback ψ Z.π PA.obj.hom jU)
    (s : S) (hs : s ∉ U)
    (hmin : ∀ t : S, t ⤳ s → t ∉ U → t = s) :
    letI : IsFinite PA.obj.hom := PA.property
    letI : QuasiCompact (c ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι :=
      MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (isPullback_morphismRestrict c U)
        (inferInstance : QuasiCompact U.ι)
    IsFinite (pullback.snd (PA.obj.hom ≫ (c ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι).fromNormalization
      (pullback.fst c (S.fromSpecStalk s)))
